question:
A 31-year-old woman visits her family physician with complaints of sharp lower back pain lasting 3
days, which began after playing intramural soccer at her college. She reports minimal relief with
naproxen. Her medical history is unremarkable. Her vital signs are as follows: | Blood pressure | 112/72
mm Hg | | --- | --- | | Heart rate | 72/min | | Respiratory rate | 12/min | | Temperature | 37.3°C (99.2°F) |
On physical examination, the patient appears mildly uncomfortable. Sensory testing and reflexes in the
lower extremities are normal (2/4 bilaterally), and muscle strength is 5/5 in both legs. An osteopathic
examination reveals a tender vertebral segment at the level of the iliac crest with a posterior right

transverse process. The asymmetry worsens on extension. What is the correct diagnosis of her
somatic dysfunction? Answer Choices: (A) L4 FSRRR (B) L5 ESLRL (C) L5 FSRRL (D) L4 ESRRR (E)
L3 FSRRL (F) L4 ESRRL (G) L4 NSRRR (H) L3 FSRRR (I) L3 ESRRR (J) L3 NSRRL
 A. L3 ESRRR
B. L3 FSRRR
C. L3 FSRRL
D. L5 FSRRL
E. L4 ESRRR
F. L4 ESRRL
G. L5 ESLRL
H. L4 FSRRR
I. L4 NSRRR
J. L3 NSRRL
